extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing manuscripts for the Annals of Probability / researchers in probability submitting to IMS journals
extracted.subtask_description: A resources-and-guidance page listing bibliographic tools, software, and English style references recommended for authors preparing submissions to the Annals of Probability (IMS). Useful for locating references, classifying papers, and preparing files for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathSciNet
rubrics_metrics.description: MathSciNet is the on-line version of Mathematical Reviews and is very useful in identifying references related to a paper. Indexing is by author, title, keywords, classification numbers, and all words in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MathSciNet to find and verify bibliographic references and to search literature by author, title, keywords, MSC classification, and review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current Index to Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Index to Statistics is a bibliographic index to publications in statistics and related fields. Indexing is by title and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Current Index to Statistics to identify statistical literature and relevant publications when preparing references and literature reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probability Abstract Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Probability Abstract Service provides abstracts of papers in probability prior to their publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this service to find recent or forthcoming probability results and abstracts that may be relevant to your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: MR Lookup
rubrics_metrics.description: MR Lookup is a convenient tool for finding the exact reference for a particular paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MR Lookup to obtain correct bibliographic details (Mathematical Reviews numbers, exact titles/authors) to ensure accurate citations in your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSC 2020 (Mathematics Subject Classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: MSC 2020 is the standard subject classification scheme used in the Annals and other major journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify your paper using MSC 2020 codes as required by the journal; choose the MSC codes that best reflect the subject areas of your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Journal Title Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Journal Title Abbreviations are provided by Mathematical Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When abbreviating journal titles in references, use the standard abbreviations provided by Mathematical Reviews to ensure consistency and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: MiKTeX (TeX program for Windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: MiKTeX is a free TeX program for Windows. It includes standard TeX and LaTeX, a dvi viewer, conversion software to produce postscript and pdf files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors preparing manuscripts on Windows can use MiKTeX to compile LaTeX sources and produce DVI/PS/PDF output compatible with journal submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghostview (PostScript viewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ghostview is a free postscript viewer available for most computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Ghostview to preview PostScript files (figures or compiled outputs) to check that typesetting and figures render correctly before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adobe Acrobat Reader (PDF viewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Adobe Acrobat Reader is a free PDF viewer available for most computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a reliable PDF reader such as Acrobat Reader to inspect the final PDF you will submit to ensure fonts, hyperlinks, and formatting are correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classic references for English usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Classic references for English usage can be found at the Great Books Online service of Bartleby.com. The references include the 1918 edition of The Elements of Style by William Strunk, Jr., the 1908 edition of The King’s English by H. W. Fowler, and the 1996 edition of the American Heritage® Book of English Usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these classic style and usage guides to improve clarity, grammar, and idiomatic English in your manuscript; follow conventional usage to meet journal editorial expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide to Grammar and Style (Jack Lynch)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide to Grammar and Style by Jack Lynch is written for students in writing classes, but provides a lot of useful information and references for other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this guide for practical advice on grammar and style when polishing exposition, particularly for clear instructional explanations or when revising for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: THE ALT.USAGE.ENGLISH FAQ FILE
rubrics_metrics.description: THE ALT.USAGE.ENGLISH FAQ FILE includes interesting discussion of English usage. If you don’t like the recommendations of the other style guides, you can probably find support for your position here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this FAQ as an informal reference for usage debates; it can provide alternate views but should be used cautiously compared to standard style manuals.
